definitions.gloss: mistletoe; parasitic plant that grows on trees
definitions.explanation: A semi-parasitic evergreen plant that grows attached to the branches of host trees, drawing water and nutrients from them.

examples.english: There's mistletoe growing on the tree branches.
In winter, mistletoe stands out on bare trees.

examples.japanese: ⟦{西洋|せいよう}→西洋：01446_seiyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦クリスマス→クリスマス：03839_kurisumasu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{宿木|やどりぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{下|した}→下：00670_shita⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦キス→キス：09763_kisu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{風習|ふうしゅう}→風習：05826_fuushuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In Western culture, there is a tradition of kissing under the mistletoe at Christmas.

notes:
The word comes from ⟦{宿|やど}→宿：03641_yado⟧ (lodging) + {木|ぎ} (tree), literally "a tree that lodges on another tree." Also written as {寄生木|やどりぎ}. In Japanese culture, {宿木|やどりぎ} is also known as a chapter title in The Tale of Genji ({源氏物語|げんじものがたり}), one of the later chapters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {宿木|やどりぎ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく: mistletoe attaches to (a tree)
- {宿木|やどりぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{実|み}→実：03741_mi⟧: mistletoe berries
- {宿木|やどりぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{下|した}→下：00670_shita⟧: under the mistletoe

BOTANICAL NOTE:
Mistletoe is a semi-parasite ({半寄生|はんきせい}) — it has green leaves and can photosynthesize, but it also draws water and minerals from the host tree through specialized roots.
